summary.text: 字 now means a written character or word, but its structure belongs to an older meaning: raising or nurturing a child. 宀 is a roof and 子 is the child beneath it. 子 also supplies sound, so the character combines a meaningful scene with a pronunciation relationship.

formation.text: The roof and child convey the older meaning together, while 子 also acts as the phonetic component.

components.text: The roof depicts the indoor setting for nurturing the child.
子 depicts the child in the scene and also provides a sound cue. Its pictorial and phonetic functions coexist.

sound.text: The syllable matches apart from tone: 子 has third tone and 字 fourth tone.
The reconstructed forms share lɯ but differ at the beginning and end. An asterisk marks a reconstruction.

history.text: Birth and nurture are attested early uses, not merely a memory aid made from the modern shape. The writing sense has been connected with characters multiplying from existing forms, using reproduction as a comparison for the production of new signs.

The sound link is visible in reconstructed Old Chinese: 字 *zlɯs and 子 *ʔslɯʔ share a similar core despite different beginnings and endings. The asterisks mark reconstructions; the pronunciation cue concerns this older relationship.

uncertainties.text: The path from nurturing to “written character” is not fully settled. A connection through producing or generating is possible, but a different word root has also been proposed. An intermediate story about education should therefore not be treated as a securely demonstrated sequence.
